stories.summary: Airstrikes Target Islamic State Positions in Somalia's Puntland Region 10 November 2026 Shabelle Media Network (Mogadishu) Bosaso — A series of airstrikes targeted suspected Islamic State positions in Somalia's northeastern Puntland region overnight, with the strikes hitting areas in Qandala district, security sources said. The bombardments mainly struck the areas of Dabablayaal and Hal Baalade, east of Dhaadaar, near key positions held by Puntland's regional security forces around the Togga Jaceel Sare area, according to local security information. The strikes were reportedly carried out by US forces supporting operations against Islamic State fighters in the Cal Miskaad mountains, where Puntland forces have been conducting a prolonged campaign against the group. There was no immediate official confirmation from US Africa Command or Puntland authorities. Security information gathered over the past four weeks indicated that Islamic State operatives, particularly members involved in operational activities and planting landmines, had been gathering in Hal Baalade and Dabablayaal, according to local sources.

"I want to tell the people of Bonchari as well, and Simba, that we are going to build that new airport," Ruto said. stories.title: Algeria: Algerian Journalist Abdelali Mezghiche Sentenced to 3 Years in Prison
stories.summary: Algerian Journalist Abdelali Mezghiche Sentenced to 3 Years in Prison HÃ©di Benyounes/Unsplash 9 November 2026 Committee to Protect Journalists (New York) New York — The Committee to Protect Journalists calls on Algerian authorities to immediately and unconditionally release journalist Abdelali Mezghiche, overturn his conviction, and stop prosecuting journalists for exercising their right to freedom of expression. On Sunday, November 8, a court in Chéraga, west of the capital Algiers, sentenced Mezghiche to three years in prison and fined him 200,000 Algerian dinars (US$1,500) on five misdemeanor charges, including publishing content deemed harmful to the national interest, inciting unarmed gatherings, and disseminating hate speech. Mezghiche's defense team plans to appeal the verdict. Prosecutors had previously sought a five-year sentence and a 200,000 Algerian dinar fine during a hearing on October 25. The judge then delivered the final verdict at the November 8 hearing. "The three-year prison sentence handed to journalist Abdelali Mezghiche for his peaceful expression is a blatant weaponization of the Algerian judiciary to silence critical voices," said CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah. "Algerian authorities must immediately release Mezghiche, overturn his conviction, and stop treating journalism as a crime." A local journalist, speaking to CPJ on condition of anonymity for fear of reprisal, said that Mezghiche was convicted under Articles 96 and 100 of Algeria's penal code, which criminalize distributing publications deemed harmful to the national interest and inciting unarmed gatherings, respectively.

stories.summary: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 10, 2026 AllAfrica AllAfrica logo 10 November 2026 allAfrica.com By Melody Chironda Nine Zimbabweans Arrested Over Alleged Russia-Ukraine War Recruitment Nine Zimbabwean nationals have been arrested in South Africa on suspicion of attempting to travel abroad to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war. The suspects, aged between 20 and 26, were arrested in Johannesburg. Five were detained at OR Tambo International Airport and four at a hotel in Bruma. stories.title: Africa's fight against fake news: Who decides what's true?
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5P8sx Prefer DW on Google In junta-run countries like Burkina Faso, fact-checking initiatives like Fasocheck are under increased government scrutiny Image: Boureima Salouka/DW Advertisement Misinformation threatens democracy worldwide: An exaggerated WhatsApp message, a manipulated TikTok video or an apparent breaking news alert on Facebook can mislead people in Africa and beyond — particularly in the run-up to elections. As artificial intelligence is making it increasingly easy to manipulate images, voices and videos, more and more countries are trying to equip their populations with skills to identify and counter fake news . But are these efforts really about raising awareness, or are certain governments using this fight to control public opinion, silence dissident voices and misguide the populace — from both within and outside of these respective nations? Civil society groups fill gaps left by governments Journalism lecturer Dani Madrid-Morales at the University of Sheffield believes that African governments must significantly step up their efforts to combat sources of disinformation and misinformation. He told DW that "there are very few countries — if any — that are actually doing a good job" of beating the influence of fake news.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Advances COP32 Preparations As COP31 Opens Amid Climate Finance Disputes
stories.summary: Ethiopia Advances COP32 Preparations As COP31 Opens Amid Climate Finance Disputes 9 November 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Ethiopia is using its participation in the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), which opened on Monday in Antalya, Türkiye, to advance preparations for hosting COP32 in Addis Abeba in November 2027, as developing countries push for stronger climate finance commitments amid widening disagreements over how to address the climate crisis. Foreign Affairs Minister Gedion Timothewos, who is also president-designate of COP32, said Ethiopia's engagement at COP31 would help establish the groundwork for a successful summit next year. Speaking about Ethiopia's participation, the state-affiliated ENA reported that Gedion outlined plans to work closely with Türkiye and Australia, which are jointly overseeing COP31, to strengthen negotiations, expand partnerships and build international participation ahead of the Addis Abeba conference. Ethiopia has opened its official pavilion in Antalya to showcase its climate mitigation efforts and engage with international partners. Gedion, who arrived in Türkiye on 8 November, is also expected to hold discussions with the COP31 presidency, negotiating groups and participating countries as Ethiopia seeks to ensure a smooth transition to its hosting responsibilities, ENA reported.

stories.title: Kenya seizes 454kg of meth in drug crackdown
stories.summary: Image source, National Police Service/X By Basillioh Rukanga Reporting from Nairobi Published 9 November 2026 Kenyan police have seized 454kg (1,000lb) of methamphetamine worth an estimated $27m (Â£20m) in an operation targeting international drug trafficking networks. Three suspects, two Tanzanians and a Ugandan, were arrested at the Kenyan coast following an intelligence-led operation involving Kenyan anti-narcotics officers and their Tanzanian counterparts. Police said the investigations began after a key suspect was arrested in Tanzania last week and handed over to Kenyan authorities at the border. Methamphetamine, commonly known as meth, is a harmful illegal synthetic drug that is highly addictive and can lead to severe psychosis, heart attack or stroke. The haul is one of the largest drug seizures in Kenya's history.

stories.summary: Rwanda: Kigali se prépare aux effets du changement climatique sur le système de santé Le ministère rwandais de la Santé a publié pour la première fois un rapport sur la vulnérabilité et l’adaptation du secteur face aux effets du changement climatique. stories.title: Africa: Africa CDC Statement On the Attack in North Kivu, DR Congo
stories.summary: Africa CDC Statement On the Attack in North Kivu, DR Congo 8 November 2026 Content from a Premium Partner Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Addis Ababa) The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) strongly condemns the deadly attack on civilians in Cantine-Aloya, North Kivu, DRC, on 5 November 2026, reportedly carried out by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF). Africa CDC extends its deepest condolences to the families of those killed and expresses its solidarity with the injured, displaced and affected communities. The attack comes at a critical moment in the response to the ongoing Ebola outbreak. Health facilities have been attacked and patients, including hundreds people with confirmed or suspected Ebola infection, have fled in search of safety raise serious public health concerns. In an Ebola outbreak, every interruption to patient care, contact tracing and disease surveillance creates additional risks for communities already facing extraordinary hardship.

stories.title: At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders estimates that for every 100 people who reach the Canary Islands by sea, 21 die during the crossing (file photo) By Ondiro Oganga Â and Â Madina Maishanu ,Â BBC Africa Published 9 November 2026 At least 39 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports. The interior ministry said one person had been rescued, but the number of people still missing was yet to be established. The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands. Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands between January and May 2026, the highest toll among the routes it monitors. Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told the AFP news agency that all the bodies recovered by Sunday evening were Senegalese.

stories.title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election
stories.summary: Image source, EPA Image caption, Voters cast their ballots at a polling station during South Africa's local government elections in Johannesburg By Ed Habershon Reporting from Johannesburg Published 8 November 2026 South Africa's ANC has recorded its worst-ever showing in local elections since Nelson Mandela led the country out of apartheid and into democracy more than 30 years ago, a result the party has called "catastrophic". While it won the most votes of all parties in the country, the African National Congress won 31% of the overall vote, one third down from the 46% it gained in 2021, and a far cry from the 65% 20 years ago. The story of its decline is also clear in the provinces and cities. The party won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo. It also won the most votes in just two of the eight cities, compared with six at the last local elections.

stories.title: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt

stories.title: Présidentielle 2027 au Nigeria : Bola Tinubu sera-t-il battu par son propre camp ?
stories.summary: Présidentielle 2027 au Nigeria : Bola Tinubu sera-t-il battu par son propre camp ? Alors que l’opposition est divisée, les principaux casse-têtes politiques du président Bola Tinubu pourraient venir de son propre camp : les ambitions rivales et les querelles entre figures influentes de l’APC menacent de compliquer sa réélection. Les candidats du Congrès des progressistes (APC) saluent leurs partisans lors du rassemblement de lancement de la campagne du parti à Kaduna, au Nigéria, le 24 octobre 2026. © Marvellous Durowaiye/REUTERS Par Oladimeji Ramon Publié aujourd'hui à 15h00, modifié à 11h59 Lecture : 5 minutes. Fichier généré le Lire dans l’app Résumer Avec une opposition nigériane fragmentée à l’approche de la présidentielle de 2027, Bola Tinubu semble partir avec une longueur d’avance. Mais, au sein de son parti, le Congrès des progressistes (APC), les ambitions rivales et les querelles personnelles entre figures puissantes menacent de compliquer sa candidature à un second mandat .

stories.title: Généraux, diplomates, politiques : au Tchad, les soldats du maréchal Déby Itno
stories.summary: Face aux crises qui secouent son environnement régional et aux fragilités de son pouvoir, Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno s’appuie sur un cercle de fidèles. Membres de sa famille, généraux, diplomates… Qui forme la garde rapprochée du président tchadien ?

stories.title: How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester
stories.summary: Daniel Oyegade on the shoot for Homage, a See My World production. Photograph: Omar Balaa View image in fullscreen Daniel Oyegade on the shoot for Homage, a See My World production. Photograph: Omar Balaa How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester . See My World , a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November. The festival is part of See My World’s year-round programme showcasing pan-African arts, culture and events.

stories.title: En RDC, ces femmes qui font l’économie
stories.summary: De l’industrie minière à la finance, cinq dirigeantes congolaises occupent des positions importantes dans l’économie de la RDC. À travers leurs parcours se dessine la place grandissante des femmes dans les centres de décision économiques du pays.

stories.title: Ebola : « Une famille ne peut pas réduire les contacts dans un logement exigu, sans eau, sans nourriture ni matériel d’hygiène »
stories.summary: Si les stratégies déployées pour limiter la propagation du virus en Afrique ne sont pas efficaces, ce n’est pas en raison de la méfiance ou du refus des populations, mais car ces dernières ne peuvent pas les mettre en œuvre, explique, dans une tribune au « Monde », le vice-président de l’ONG Alima Thierry Allafort-Duverger.

stories.title: À Dakar, les soirées 100 % féminines ont la cote et bousculent les codes
stories.summary: Depuis plus d’un an, dans la capitale sénégalaise, le concept « Yaay sort danser » réunit chaque trimestre un nombre croissant de participantes. Elles peuvent écouter de la musique et danser librement, sans peur d’être jugées, sans danger.

stories.title: Coumba Ba, candidate mauritanienne à l’OIF : « Je serai la secrétaire générale du consensus »
stories.summary: À quelques jours du sommet de l’Organisation internationale de la francophonie, qui se tiendra du 14 au 16 novembre à Phnom Penh, au Cambodge, la Mauritanienne poursuit discrètement sa campagne. Et croit toujours en ses chances.

stories.title: South Africa’s Politics May Never Be the Same Again
stories.summary: The African National Congress lost big in local elections, turning a once-dominant force credited with overturning apartheid into “any other political party.”

stories.title: Ebola: Why is there still no vaccine?
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5PCYI Prefer DW on Google Researchers are working to develop a vaccine against the strain of Ebola responsible for the current outbreak Image: Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement 1976: A hitherto unknown disease breaks out near the Ebola river in the country then known as Zaire, now the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This was the first scientifically documented Ebola epidemic. Now, 50 years on, the DRC once again finds itself at the center of a major Ebola outbreak . This time the pathogen is the less common Bundibugyo type of the genus orthoebolavirus. The virus was identified in 2007 during an outbreak in Bundibugyo, Uganda .

stories.title: Islamist Militant Attack Forces Patients to Flee Ebola Clinic in Congo
stories.summary: At least 48 people were killed in a brutal assault by a group loyal to the Islamic State, officials said. The area is a hot spot of the growing Ebola outbreak.

stories.title: « Ils l’ignorent parce qu’il est invisible » : El Niño, le grand oublié des élections au Nigeria
stories.summary: Frappé par des chaleurs extrêmes dues à El Niño, le nord du Nigeria voit ses récoltes et son bétail dépérir. Pourtant, à l’approche de la présidentielle de 2027, la classe politique passe ce péril majeur sous silence.

stories.title: Chris Coons, l’africaniste qui prend les commandes de la diplomatie au Sénat américain
stories.summary: Réélu pour un quatrième mandat, le sénateur démocrate du Delaware devrait prendre la tête de la puissante commission des Affaires étrangères du Sénat. Portrait de cet ancien militant anti-apartheid et fin connaisseur du continent, qui a bâti sa carrière sur la discrétion et le compromis.

stories.title: VIH : le générique du lénacapavir, un médicament qui promet de révolutionner la lutte contre le virus du sida, prêt à être commercialisé
stories.summary: L’agence américaine du médicament a donné son feu vert à la mise sur le marché de ce traitement, beaucoup moins contraignant que celui utilisé jusque-là. Une avancée majeure en matière de prévention, en particulier pour le continent africain, le plus touché par la pandémie.

stories.title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Somalia has the longest coastline in mainland Africa By Fardowsa Hanshi BBC Somali Published 7 November 2026 As the sun rises over the Indian Ocean, waves lap onto the golden sands while palm fronds rustle in the cool sea breeze. This is the image that one young Somali woman wants the world to have of her home city - in contrast to the one of suicide attacks and young men wielding AK-47s that many people currently associate with Somalia's capital. Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader is among a growing number of local guides taking visitors beyond the headlines to explore Mogadishu's beauty spots, historic sites and culture. Her favourite spot is Jazeera beach, where visitors can enjoy the sea before heading to nearby sand dunes. "It's one of the tourist attractions where we bring our guests. It's a nice place," says the 23-year-old.

stories.title: Kenya Cult Leader Handed 200 Year Prison Sentence for Mass Murder
stories.summary: Paul Nthenge Mackenzie told followers to starve themselves in order to meet Jesus, an edict that was violently enforced, a court heard during his trial.

stories.title: Tanzania’s Opposition Leader Gets a Four-Year Sentence
stories.summary: Tundu Lissu was found guilty of incitement for statements he had made ahead of a presidential election in October 2025.

stories.title: En Ethiopie, le pari perdu de Debretsion Gebremichael, chef de la rébellion tigréenne
stories.summary: Ce discret cacique du Front populaire de libération du Tigré, un temps ministre à Addis-Abeba, a ravivé les hostilités avec le pouvoir fédéral, fin septembre. Ses troupes ont été chassées de leur fief de Makalé.

stories.title: En Afrique du Sud, l’ANC subit son plus sévère recul électoral : « Les électeurs noirs votent sur les compétences plus que sur le passé ou la couleur de peau »
stories.summary: Le parti de Nelson Mandela devrait rester le premier du pays, avec 31,7 % des voix, contre 25,8 % pour l’Alliance démocratique, son principal concurrent, lors des élections municipales du 4 novembre. Mais la formation, qui a longtemps rassemblé plus de 60 % des suffrages, réalise le score le plus bas de son histoire.

stories.title: A Makalé, capitale d’un Tigré retombé aux mains de l’armée éthiopienne, l’écho persistant de la guerre
stories.summary: La ville a été reprise par l’armée fédérale le 3 octobre. Chassés de leur fief historique, les rebelles tigréens se sont retranchés dans les zones montagneuses de la région. Le retour du conflit ravive les blessures de la guerre de 2020, au cours de laquelle Makalé avait subi un siège et des crimes de guerre.

stories.title: Kehinde Wiley Will Debut New Art Series
stories.summary: The artist, who has been facing sexual misconduct allegations, became a single father in May and returns to the gallery world this week with a new show, “What the Light Becomes.”

stories.title: Au Nigeria, Atiku Abubakar maintient sa candidature à la présidentielle malgré l’annulation par la justice
stories.summary: Jeudi, un tribunal d’Abuja a annulé la candidature de celui qui brigue pour la septième fois la magistrature suprême en invalidant toutes les décisions prises par le président de sa formation politique, le Congrès démocratique africain (ADC), jugé illégitime.

stories.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children
stories.summary: Mackenzie, a former taxi driver, forbade cult members from sending their children to school and from going to hospital when they were ill. Photograph: EPA View image in fullscreen Mackenzie, a former taxi driver, forbade cult members from sending their children to school and from going to hospital when they were ill. Photograph: EPA Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history. The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes. Prosecutors said Paul Mackenzie and his Good News International church ran ​a Christian doomsday sect whose members were ordered to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended.

stories.title: Who’s Hiding Secrets About Dag Hammarskjöld’s Death?

stories.title: Municipales en Afrique du Sud, JOJ Dakar 2026, Midterms pour l'Afrique : l'hebdo Afrique
stories.summary: Publicité Récap Municipales en Afrique du Sud, JOJ Dakar 2026, Midterms pour l'Afrique : l'hebdo Afrique Publié le : 06/11/2026 - 13:50 6 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Un homme vote lors des élections locales dans la commune d'Alexandra, à la périphérie de Johannesburg, en Afrique du Sud, le 4 novembre 2026. © Themba Hadebe, AP Les Sud-Africains se sont rendus aux urnes, mercredi, pour les élections municipales – dernière échéance électorale avant le scrutin général de 2029 –, au terme d'une campagne centrée sur la crise des services publics. Le Congrès national africain (ANC), à la tête de l'Afrique du Sud depuis 1994, se dirige vers le pire résultat électoral de son histoire, d'après le dépouillement de 80% des votes. Le maintien au pouvoir du président somalien Hassan Sheikh Mohamud est "illégal", car l'adoption d'une nouvelle Constitution en mars dernier, qui a prolongé de quatre à cinq ans le mandat présidentiel, ne pouvait s'appliquer à son mandat actuel, a tranché jeudi la Cour suprême somalienne. La plus haute juridiction somalienne a, par ailleurs, déclaré "nulle", dans une décision séparée, l'annonce mercredi sur Facebook par le chef de l'État de démettre de ses fonctions le président de la Cour suprême Bashe Yusuf Ahmed. La justice nigériane a annulé, jeudi, la candidature de l'ancien vice-président et opposant Atiku Abubakar au scrutin présidentiel de janvier, au lendemain du lancement officiel de sa campagne électorale.

stories.title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Like many neighbouring countries, Guinea-Bissau waits until babies are six weeks old to vaccinate them against hepatitis B, while the WHO says it should be done at birth (file photo) By Basma El Atti Â and Â Makuochi Okafor ,Â BBC Africa Published 5 November 2026 A proposed trial of a hepatitis B vaccine on newborn babies in Guinea-Bissau has been cancelled following accusations that the trial was "unethical" and "neocolonial". The trial was funded by the US, under Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has a long record of expressing scepticism about vaccines. Police have seized a batch of vaccines from the research centre at the heart of the controversy. The proposed trial drew international criticism because it planned to withhold a vaccine recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) from half of the participating newborns. Some public health experts argued that the proposed trial raised broader questions about whether vulnerable populations in African countries were being asked to take risks that researchers would not accept in wealthier countries.

stories.summary: The maternal drape, as it is called, is helping to solve one of the world’s most intractable health problems.

stories.title: British healthcare worker with Ebola evacuated from DR Congo to UK
stories.summary: The patient, whose identity was not disclosed, had been sent to DR Congo by a humanitarian organisation to help support the response to the outbreak. Photograph: Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/AP View image in fullscreen The patient, whose identity was not disclosed, had been sent to DR Congo by a humanitarian organisation to help support the response to the outbreak. Photograph: Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/AP British healthcare worker with Ebola evacuated from DR Congo to UK Patient is ⁠in ​stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist ‘high consequence’ infectious disease unit A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed. “A British citizen currently in the DR Congo has tested positive for Ebola ,” a spokesperson for the UK government said in a statement on Wednesday. “The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated … The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.” The patient, whose identity is unknown, is in a stable condition and is expected to arrive in the UK on Wednesday or Thursday before being transferred in a specialist ambulance to a “high consequence” infectious disease unit, according to an official document seen by Reuters. A humanitarian organisation sent the worker to DR Congo to help in the response to the outbreak, which is the second largest on record. It is the first case involving a British national contracting Ebola in the current outbreak.

stories.title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms
stories.summary: Figure caption, Watch: Abdul El-Sayed thanks supporters for backing 'unlikeliest of candidates' By Basma El Atti Published 4 November 2026 "JD [Vance], habibi (my love)". It was an unlikely greeting to hear at a Democratic Party victory rally after the US midterm elections. Abdul El-Sayed , 42, born to Egyptian immigrant parents, playfully addressed Vice-President JD Vance, who had campaigned against him but will now swear him into office in January as Michigan's new Senator. The US-born Democrat spent much of his campaign fending off attacks from conservative media and President Donald Trump, who accused him of supporting the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed rejected the allegations. "My name is Abdul Rahman Mohammed El-Sayed," he said in an Egyptian Arabic accent to the cheering crowd at his victory rally.

stories.title: ANC faces anger over poor services as South Africans vote in local elections
stories.summary: A voter casts their ballot in Lawley township, south of Johannesburg, South Africa. Photograph: Oupa Nkosi/Reuters ANC faces anger over poor services as South Africans vote in local elections Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure. The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party. However, polls showed it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the last municipal elections in 2021 and 40.2% in 2024’s national elections .

stories.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, More than 500 parties are contesting the elections By Khanyisile Ngcobo Reporting from Johannesburg Published 4 November 2026 South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC). This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes. Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations. Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection. For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern.

stories.summary: Image source, Anadolu via Getty Images Image caption, Rwanda's army team APR came third in the Basketball Africa League last year By Basillioh Rukanga Published 4 November 2026 The National Basketball Association (NBA) says it removed Rwanda's army team from its African league because of US sanctions imposed on the country in March. The NBA had previously said the Rwandan army-funded ArmÃ©e Patriotique Rwandaise (APR) club would not participate in the 2026 Basketball Africa League (BAL). stories.title: Can an African feminist have a white wedding? It’s complicated | Patience Akumu
stories.summary: Patience and Mark at their wedding. ‘Getting married as an African feminist felt like the pope renouncing Catholicism – uncomfortable and unlikely.’ Photograph: Courtesy of Patience Akumu View image in fullscreen Patience and Mark at their wedding. ‘Getting married as an African feminist felt like the pope renouncing Catholicism – uncomfortable and unlikely.’ Photograph: Courtesy of Patience Akumu Can an African feminist have a white wedding? It’s complicated Patience Akumu I wanted to be a beacon of black feminist love; my friends and family teased me for being a sellout W e had been together 20 years, had two children and had a customary marriage with our village sub-county two years ago without any real plans for a church wedding. So we called our second ceremony a celebration of love and not a wedding. How else would a self-professed African feminist survive being the centre of a colonial and Abrahamic religious ceremony that also manages to reinforce the most male-centred aspects of African culture? Our invitations came directly from me and my partner Mark, not – as is traditional – from our families, and in the form of a playful gif featuring the song Love Potion from the South African group Mafikizolo, a reminder that this was a wedding on our terms.
